lines.en: I heard a great story recently -- I love telling it -- of a little girl who was in a drawing lesson.
lines.zh: 有個小女孩在上繪畫課。她六歲，

lines.zh: 老師說這小女孩平常非常難專注在

lines.en: and in this drawing lesson, she did. The teacher was fascinated.

lines.zh: 問道：妳在畫什麼？

lines.en: (Laughter) "Nativity II."

lines.en: What these things have in common is that kids will take a chance.

lines.en: If they don't know, they'll have a go.

lines.en: Am I right? They're not frightened of being wrong.
lines.zh: 我說的對吧？他們不怕犯錯。

lines.en: I don't mean to say that being wrong is the same thing as being creative.
lines.zh: 當然，我不是說犯錯等於有創意。

lines.en: What we do know is, if you're not prepared to be wrong,
lines.zh: 如果你沒有犯錯的心理準備，

lines.en: you'll never come up with anything original --
lines.zh: 就永遠無法發揮獨創性。

lines.en: if you're not prepared to be wrong.
lines.zh: 如果你都不準備犯錯。當他們長大成人時，

lines.en: And by the time they get to be adults, most kids have lost that capacity.

lines.en: They have become frightened of being wrong.
lines.zh: 他們會變得害怕犯錯。

lines.en: And we run our companies like this.

lines.en: So why is this? I lived in Stratford-on-Avon until about five years ago.
lines.zh: 我以前住在英國埃文河畔的斯特拉福， 莎士比亞的家鄉。

lines.en: In fact, we moved from Stratford to Los Angeles. So you can imagine what a seamless transition this was.
lines.zh: 所以你可以了解，這是個多麼平順的轉變吧。

lines.en: (Laughter)
lines.zh: （笑聲）事實上，

lines.en: Actually, we lived in a place called Snitterfield,
lines.zh: 我們那時住在斯特拉福外圍的

lines.en: just outside Stratford,
lines.zh: 斯尼特菲爾，那是

lines.en: which is where Shakespeare's father was born. Are you struck by a new thought? I was.

lines.zh: 想過嗎？因為你沒有想過

lines.zh: （笑聲）「你得更用功」 爸爸趕他上床睡覺，你知道的，

lines.zh: （笑聲）

lines.en: Anyway, we moved from Stratford to Los Angeles,
lines.zh: 反正呢，我們從斯特拉福搬到洛城，

lines.en: and I just want to say a word about the transition. Actually, my son didn't want to come.

lines.zh: 他不想來洛杉磯。他很喜歡這裡，

lines.en: This was the love of his life, Sarah.
lines.zh: 他那時認識她一個月。

lines.zh: 告訴你，他們好像已經認識四年一樣，

lines.en: And we were rather pleased about that, frankly -- (Laughter) because she was the main reason we were leaving the country.

lines.en: (Laughter)
lines.zh: （笑聲）

lines.en: But something strikes you when you move to America
lines.zh: 或是在世界各地旅行時

lines.en: and travel around the world: every education system on earth has the same hierarchy of subjects.
lines.zh: 你會驚訝的發現，這地球上所有教育系統 都有同樣的科目階級制度。

lines.en: Every one. Doesn't matter where you go.
lines.zh: 你以為會有所不同，但真的沒有差別。

lines.en: You'd think it would be otherwise, but it isn't.

lines.en: At the top are mathematics and languages, then the humanities.

lines.en: At the bottom are the arts. Everywhere on earth.
lines.zh: 到處都一樣。

lines.en: And in pretty much every system, too, there's a hierarchy within the arts.
lines.zh: 而且每個教育體系中的藝術課程中，

lines.zh: 美術和音樂課程在學校永遠比

lines.en: than drama and dance. There isn't an education system on the planet
lines.zh: 戲劇和舞蹈課程更重要。 這地球上沒有一個教育系統

lines.en: that teaches dance every day to children
lines.zh: 每天教授小孩們跳舞，

lines.en: Why? Why not?

lines.en: I think this is rather important. I think math is very important, but so is dance.

lines.en: Children dance all the time if they're allowed to, we all do.

lines.en: We all have bodies, don't we? Did I miss a meeting?

lines.en: (Laughter)
lines.zh: （笑聲）這一切背後的真相是，
